trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out right, up, left or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: right.
The line must go up: right is number 11, which comes later; down is number 13, which comes later.
I can't rule out left or up yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going to number 3, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So my guess (left from cell (4,3)) was wrong, so the line must go up.
Going up, the next 7 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,2). So the line goes left.
The line must go down: up is number 15, which comes later; left is number 6, which comes later.
Going around the edge to (4,6) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down.
Number 4 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going around the edge to (1,1) leaves no safe move afterwards; going right, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,1). So the line goes around the edge to (6,6).
Number 5 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going left would leave number 6 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes up.
The line must go up: left is number 10, which comes later.

Going up would strand number 6: it would be left with only one free neighbour; going left would strand number 6: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes around the edge to (3,1).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going around the edge to (2,6), the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at number 7. So the line goes up.
Number 7 is only reachable this way.
Cell (2,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going down would leave number 8 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going left, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,4). So the line goes up.
The line must go left: around the edge to (6,5) is number 12, which comes later.
Going around the edge to (6,4) would force the line onto number 12 before its turn. So the line goes down.
Number 9 is only reachable this way.
Cell (3,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (4,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (5,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (6,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes around the edge to (1,2).
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
